# The purpose of this script is to

1.  Import, and clean the Jenn Fields' timeseries tide pool data
2.  Summarize the mean and standard deviation of the Temperature and Light Intensity of each tide pool.
3.  In both base R for loops and Purr map() functions.

## Loading Libraries

```{r}
#| message: FALSE
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
```

## Importing Data

```{r}
tp_path <- here("Week_13","data","homework") #making the file path an object

files <- dir(path = tp_path, pattern = ".csv") #using the object with pattern to pull all .csv from that path

files #display that all the file names are in an object
```

PoolID 4 is the Control

# For Loop-ing

## Pre-allocating loop space

```{r}
# One row for each file and 3 columns
tp_data <- tibble(tide_pool_ID = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    mean_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    sd_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    mean_lux = rep(NA, length(files)),
                    sd_lux = rep(NA, length(files)))

tp_data
```

## For({})

```{r}
#| message: FALSE
for (i in seq_along(files)) {

  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(tp_path, "/", files[i]))

  tp_data$tide_pool_ID[i] <- files[i]
  tp_data$mean_temp[i] <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE) #Calculates Mean temp of each Tide Pool
  tp_data$sd_temp[i] <- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE) #Calculates the standard deviation of that temp
  tp_data$mean_lux[i] <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE) #Calculates Mean Lux of each Tide Pool
  tp_data$sd_lux[i] <- sd(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE) #Calculates the standard deviation of that Lux
}

tp_data
```

Wow, we can see that the Control (TP4) and the TP1 have lower mean light intensities than TP2 and 3, something to keep in mind when analyzing the data further. Temperature seems to be pretty close otherwise, with all the SDs overlapping each mean_temp.

# With purr's map()

## Alt method to reading in files

```{r}
files2 <- dir(path = tp_path, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE) # saves the entire path
files2
```

## map() code

```{r}
#| message: FALSE
tp_data2 <- files2 |>
  set_names() |>
  map(read_csv) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "filename") |>
  group_by(PoolID) |>
#Did this one by PoolID to confirm that each file is its own pool
  summarize(mean_temp = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_temp = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_lux = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_lux = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE))

tp_data2

```

# Output

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tide
#| tbl-cap: "Tidial Pool Means and SDs for C and Lux"
#| tbl-subcap: 
#|   - "For Loop method" 
#|   - "map() method"

kable(tp_data)
kable(tp_data2)
```

There's no difference between grouping by file name @tbl-tide-1, and by PoolID @tbl-tide-2.
